open_points.subject: sandbox time-entry-point trap classification
open_points.kind: changed rule lacks matching module fact
open_points.text: A03 now traps `time.localtime`, `time.gmtime`, `time.ctime` and `time.asctime` “when called without an argument or with `None`”, while State 3 exposes only `data_provider.SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT` and says `sandbox_runner` installs traps from those provider lists.
open_points.question: Which module owns and exposes the new distinction that these four entry points must also trap an explicit `None`, and how is `sandbox_runner` to obtain it without silently redefining `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT` or hard-coding a second policy fact?
options: Redefine `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT` to mean calls with no argument or `None` despite its name
Add a separate data-provider classification for calls with no argument or `None`
Have `sandbox_runner` special-case these four functions independently of the provider lists
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate data-provider classification consumed by `sandbox_runner`.

witness.initial: An admitted implementation calls `time.localtime(None)`, catches any exception, and returns a conforming value.
events: The kernel executes the implementation in the sandbox.
One implementer builds traps strictly from `SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT`; another treats the changed A03 phrase as requiring an explicit-`None` trap despite the State 3 capability taxonomy.
outcomes: The call with `None` is not classified by the provider fact, so it returns the current local time and the execution can succeed.
The call records a trap hit and the execution concludes `sandbox_violation` even though the implementation catches the exception.
witness.observer: The agent or owner inspecting the trial or run outcome.
